subject: biochemistry
title: Hemoglobin and myoglobin: cooperativity, allosteric effectors, 2,3-BPG and the Bohr effect

steps.tx: Myoglobin and hemoglobin exhibit contrasting oxygen-binding **curves** suited to their distinct physiological niches. Monomeric myoglobin displays a hyperbolic binding curve with high oxygen affinity, releasing oxygen only at low tissue partial pressures during muscle hypoxia. In contrast, tetrameric hemoglobin exhibits a sigmoidal curve reflecting positive cooperativity, allowing efficient oxygen loading in alveolar capillaries and unloading in peripheral tissues.
steps.say: Myoglobin and hemoglobin curves reflect their distinct biological functions. Monomeric myoglobin shows a hyperbolic curve with high oxygen affinity, releasing oxygen only during tissue hypoxia. Tetrameric hemoglobin displays a sigmoidal curve from cooperativity, loading oxygen in lungs and releasing it in tissues.

left.title: Myoglobin properties
points: Single polypeptide chain with one heme
Very low P50 of 2 to 3 mmHg

right.title: Hemoglobin properties
points: Tetramer of two alpha and two beta chains
P50 of 26 to 27 mmHg under normal conditions
Regulated by pH, CO2, temperature and 2,3-BPG

steps.tx: Oxygen binding induces transition between two quaternary **conformations**: the tense T-state and the relaxed R-state. Deoxygenated hemoglobin is constrained in the T-state by multiple inter-subunit salt bridges. Binding of oxygen to iron pulls the protoporphyrin ring flat, shifting the proximal histidine and rotating the alpha-beta dimers fifteen degrees. This rupture of salt bridges stabilizes the high-affinity R-state.
steps.say: Hemoglobin transitions between tense T and relaxed R states. Deoxygenated hemoglobin adopts the T state stabilized by ionic salt bridges. Oxygen binding pulls the heme iron into the porphyrin plane, tilting the proximal histidine and rotating dimers into the high-affinity R state.

steps.tx: The **Bohr effect** facilitates reciprocal oxygen delivery and carbon dioxide clearance. In metabolically active tissues, elevated carbon dioxide hydration generates carbonic acid, dissociating into protons. Protons bind specific histidine residues on beta chains, stabilizing the T-state and right-shifting the dissociation curve. This right-shift increases oxygen unloading. In pulmonary capillaries, oxygenation displaces protons and carbon dioxide, a phenomenon termed the Haldane effect.
steps.say: The Bohr effect coordinates oxygen release with carbon dioxide transport. Metabolically active tissues generate protons that bind histidine residues, stabilizing the low-affinity T state and shifting the curve rightward. In lungs, oxygen binding releases carbon dioxide via the Haldane effect.

rows: Extracts oxygen across placenta from HbA

steps.tx: The organic phosphate **2,3-BPG** is synthesized via the Rapoport-Luebering glycolytic shunt in red blood cells. A single molecule binds the central cavity of the T-state tetramer, forming ionic bonds with positively charged lysine and histidine residues on both beta chains. Fetal hemoglobin replaces beta chains with gamma chains containing serine-143 instead of histidine-143, decreasing 2,3-BPG affinity and facilitating transplacental oxygen transfer.
steps.say: 2,3-BPG is produced by the Rapoport-Luebering shunt in red blood cells. It nests within the central cavity of the deoxygenated T-state tetramer. Fetal hemoglobin replaces beta chain histidine-143 with serine, lowering 2,3-BPG binding and enabling fetal oxygen uptake across the placenta.
